To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

single-ISA heterogeneous architectures provide significant performance benefits over homogeneous architectures for multithreading workloads, and that dynamic core assignment policies can achieve these benefits.
a single-ISA heterogeneous architecture is more effective than a homogeneous one, and that a heterogeneous architecture that includes a multithreaded core is more effective than one without.

1) Single-ISA heterogeneous multi-cores are a promising architecture for multithread workloads; 2) A heterogeneous architecture can outperform the same area homogeneous architecture by up 63%; and 3) Dynamic core assignment policies can provide significant performance gains, and even outperformed the best static assignment policy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to design a chip multiprocessors that can provide high performance for a wide variety of workloads, and how to assign threads to cores to achieve that performance.
the design of a single-ISA heterogeneous multiprocessor, and the design of a dynamic core assignment policy to exploit its benefits.
the design, implementation and performance analysis of a single-ISA heterogeneous architecture.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
single-ISA heterogeneous architectures are a promising direction for chip multiprocessor design.
a heterogeneous single-ISA multi-core architecture can provide significantly better performance in the same die area than a comparable homogeneous architecture.

the heterogeneous multi-core is an attractive architecture that provides significant performance gains over a homogeneous one, and that the performance of such an architecture is sensitive to the assignment policy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the heterogeneous architecture is the better choice for the majority of workloads.
a single-ISA heterogeneous chip multiprocessor provides a better match for a multithreaded, diverse workload than a conventional, homogeneous chip multiprocessor does.
a heterogeneous multi-core processor can be a very good choice to achieve better performance for a diverse workload, especially when the workload is highly multithreaded.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance benefits of a single-ISA heterogeneous architecture are not limited to specific applications, but can be achieved across a wide range of workloads.
heterogeneous architectures can provide a significant performance advantage for a diverse set of workloads.
heterogeneous multi-core architectures can provide significantly better performance than homogeneous architectures, and that dynamic policies can outperform static ones by a large amount.
